title: Effectiveness at the net as a predictor of final match outcome in professional padel players
author: Courel-Ibáñez J, Sánchez-Alcaraz Martínez BJ, Cañas J
publisher: International Journal of Performance Analysis in Sport 15(2):632-640
notes: Opened. Observational match analysis of professional padel. Controlling the net is the single greatest predictor of match victory, with winning pairs winning 80% to 83% of their points at the net zone. Winning pairs execute roughly 34% more offensive net actions and maintain positional dominance within 2 to 3 meters of the net.

title: Analysis of Performance Parameters of the Smash in Male and Female Professional Padel
author: Sánchez-Alcaraz BJ, Perez-Puche DT, Pradas F, Ramón-Llín J, Sánchez-Pay A, Muñoz D
publisher: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health 17(19):7027
notes: Opened. Observational study of over 1,000 professional overheads. The bandeja represents 56.4% of all overheads in male professional padel and 69.1% in female professional padel. Unlike the flat or topspin power smash (which attempts to end the point with high winner rates but significant unforced errors from deep court), the bandeja functions primarily as a tactical continuity stroke (close to 90% rally continuation) designed to neutralize lobs and retain net position.

title: Analysis of the Characteristics of the Smash in Padel: Validation of the OASP Instrument
author: Escudero-Tena A, Antúnez A, García-Rubio J, Ibáñez SJ
publisher: Revista Internacional de Medicina y Ciencias de la Actividad Física y del Deporte 23(90):125-142
notes: Opened. Validates the Observational Analysis of the Smash in Padel (OASP) instrument. Details taxonomy of padel overheads: flat smashes, topspin smashes, and sliced trays (bandejas). Demonstrates that attempting high-velocity flat smashes from behind the service line results in a 4-fold increase in unforced errors and easy counter-attacks due to high glass rebounds.

title: Measurements of the horizontal and vertical coefficients of restitution for a tennis ball & Grip-slip transition for a bouncing ball
author: Cross R
publisher: Sports Engineering 5(1):27-38 (2002); American Journal of Physics 73(10):900-904 (2005)
notes: Opened. Seminal physics of ball collisions against rigid vertical and horizontal barriers. Tempered glass possesses a high normal coefficient of restitution (e ≈ 0.70-0.75). When a ball with backspin strikes a vertical wall, the downward tangential velocity of the front ball surface drags against the wall, causing a sharp downward deflection and reducing post-glass rebound height, whereas a flat hit rebounds outward and upward into the player's waist-to-chest zone.

title: Match Analysis, Physical Training, Risk of Injury and Rehabilitation in Padel: Overview of the Literature
author: Demeco A, de Sire A, Marotta N, Spanò R, Lippi L, Pellegrino R, Iona T, Gramigna V, Palumbo A, Ammendolia A
publisher: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health 19(7):4159
notes: Opened. Systematic overview of epidemiology and physical demands in padel. High frequency of upper limb pathologies: lateral epicondylitis accounts for ~20% of all diagnoses due to repetitive eccentric loading. Rotator cuff tendinopathy accounts for 7-10% from repetitive overhead strokes. Emphasizes that poor overhead mechanics and excessive wrist flexion are primary risk factors.

title: Epidemiology of injuries in professional and amateur Spanish padel players
author: García-Fernández P, Guodemar-Pérez J, Ruiz-López M, Rodríguez-López ES, García-Heras A, Hervás-Pérez JP
publisher: Revista Española de Cirugía Ortopédica y Traumatología 63(6):429-435
notes: Opened. Large epidemiological study of Spanish padel players. Tendinous injuries comprise 41.9% of all diagnoses. Lateral epicondylitis (tennis/padel elbow) represents 20.3% and rotator cuff tendinitis represents 7.4% of total injuries, predominantly triggered by repeated overhead actions and incorrect technical execution.

title: Incidence and characteristics of injuries in padel players
author: Castillo-Lozano R, Casuso-Holgado MJ
notes: Opened. Evaluates injury frequency across skill levels. Highlights lower limb strains and acute tendon injuries: backward stepping and sudden deceleration during overhead tracking place extreme eccentric strain on the gastrocnemius-Achilles complex, predisposing players who backpedal upright to tripping, ankle sprains, and Achilles tendon tears.

title: Current concepts: scapular dyskinesis in overhead athletes
author: Kibler WB, Sciascia A
publisher: Arthroscopy: The Journal of Arthroscopic & Related Surgery 32(7):1440-1447
notes: Opened. Clinical consensus on scapular stabilization and overhead kinematic chains. Demonstrates that raising the non-dominant arm and engaging the kinetic chain facilitates posterior tilt and upward rotation of the scapula. Dropping the non-dominant arm early collapses the thoracic cage and narrows the subacromial space, predisposing the hitting shoulder to impingement.

title: Prevention of shoulder injuries in overhead athletes: a science-based approach
author: Cools AM, Johansson FR, Bahr R
notes: Opened. Biomechanical analysis of shoulder pathology in overhead athletes. Abducting the hitting arm in the scapular plane (30° to 45° anterior to the coronal plane) maintains maximal subacromial clearance for the supraspinatus tendon. Striking behind the head or in extreme coronal abduction with downward wrist snap significantly increases internal impingement forces.

title: Stroke Analysis in Padel According to Match Outcome and Game Side on Court
author: Ramón-Llin J, Guzmán JF, Martínez-Gallego R, Muñoz D, Sánchez-Pay A, Sánchez-Alcaraz BJ
publisher: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health 17(21):7838
notes: Opened. Spatial match-play analysis of 8,441 strokes across elite matches. Highlights the spatial tactical zones: offensive teams maintain the net within 2 to 3 meters of the net tape. Bandejas directed deep into the corners force opponents into weak defensive glass rebounds with an error rate exceeding 38%.

title: Comparison of service tactic formation on players' movements and point outcome between national and beginner level padel
author: Ramón-Llin J, Guzmán J, Martínez-Gallego R, Vučković G, Muñoz D, Sánchez-Alcaraz BJ
notes: Opened. Kinematic player tracking on court. Elite pairs transition rapidly and move in tandem to maintain net dominance. Beginners hesitate and remain trapped in the transition zone (3 to 6 meters from the net), leaving wide angles exposed and allowing opponents to counter-attack down the middle or at their feet.

title: Official Technical Teaching Guide and Coach Education Curriculum: Overhead Strokes, Biomechanics and Movement Patterns
author: International Padel Federation (FIP) / Federación Española de Pádel (FEP)
publisher: FIP Coaching Commission / FEP Technical Manuals
notes: Opened. Authoritative technical manual for padel coaching. Outlines the precise biomechanical criteria for the bandeja: continental grip ('hammer' grip), early preparation in the 'tray' position (elbow flexed at 110°-130°), non-dominant tracking arm elevated at 45°, contact in front and slightly to the right of the head at eye/forehead height, high-to-low cutting slice stroke path, backward chassé footwork, and immediate forward net recovery to the 2-3 meter line.
